cards.what_happened: The Colombo Harbour Police began an investigation after an unidentified male body was found floating in the sea near the Boat House Jetty. The man was estimated to be approximately 45 years old and was wearing brown shorts and a black T-shirt. Police are investigating whether the death was a homicide or another incident.
details: The Newswire reported that the Colombo Harbour Police launched an investigation after an unidentified male body was found floating in the sea near the Boat House Jetty in Colombo Harbour. According to Police, the body was discovered yesterday morning (18), following information received about a body floating in the water.

The identity of the deceased has not yet been established. Police estimate that the man was approximately 45 years old and was wearing brown shorts and a black T-shirt at the time of discovery. The Colombo Harbour Police are conducting further investigations to determine whether the death was a homicide or resulted from another incident.

Suspect arrested over assault on bus driver in Dambulla

cards.what_happened: A suspect has been arrested over the assault of a private bus driver in Dambulla. The attack happened on November 14 in front of the main bus stand, and footage of it circulated on social media. The suspect, from Pohoranwewa in Dambulla, was arrested yesterday (18) and is to be produced before court today (19).
details: Police say the assault took place on November 14 in front of the main bus stand in Dambulla. It involved the driver of a private bus travelling from Kandy to Polonnaruwa, who was injured in the attack.
The injured driver lodged a complaint with Police while receiving treatment at the Dambulla Hospital. The arrest came after footage of the incident circulated on social media.

After investigations, officers of the Dambulla Headquarters Police used CCTV footage of the incident to identify the suspect. The suspect, a resident of Pohoranwewa in Dambulla, was arrested yesterday (18).
He is scheduled to be produced before court today (19). The Dambulla Headquarters Police are conducting further investigations.

Officers of the Dambulla Headquarters Police used CCTV footage to identify the suspect, a resident of Pohoranwewa in Dambulla, who was arrested yesterday, the 18th. Haitian Prime Minister commends Sri Lankan troops for successful anti-gang operation

cards.what_happened: Sri Lankan troops serving with the international Gang Suppression Force joined Haiti's National Police in a pre-dawn raid on November 15 against the Kokorat San Ras gang in Gros-Morne, Artibonite. The joint forces freed a church and a school held by gang members, seized weapons and motorcycles, and cleared roads blocked for years. Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised the operation on X.
details: On November 15, Sri Lankan personnel serving under the international Gang Suppression Force (GSF) took part in a joint anti-gang operation with the Haitian National Police (PNH) in the Artibonite region. The pre-dawn raid targeted strongholds of the armed Kokorat San Ras gang in the Tibwadòm and Carnifice areas of Gros-Morne.

During the mission, the joint forces cleared and secured a church and a school that gang members had occupied. They seized firearms, ammunition, and motorcycles, and dismantled barricades and trenches that were blocking National Road 5. This cleared key roadways that had been blocked for years.

Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé praised the coordinated operation in a post on X, commending the PNH, GSF and Sri Lankan troops. Sri Lankan personnel are stationed across key operational hubs including Port-au-Prince, Gonaïves, and Estrella. There they conduct armoured vehicle patrols, safeguard vital supply routes, and support local authorities in dismantling organized crime networks and restoring stability for affected civilian communities.
cards.why_it_matters: The raid reopened roads that had been blocked for years and helped restore stability for local communities affected by gangs.

cards.spoken: Sri Lankan soldiers serving in Haiti have earned praise from the country's Prime Minister after a big anti-gang mission. On November fifteenth, these troops, part of an international Gang Suppression Force, joined Haiti's National Police for a pre-dawn raid in the Artibonite region. They targeted a gang called Kokorat San Ras in the Gros-Morne area. During the operation, the forces took back a church and a school that gang members had occupied, seized guns, ammunition and motorcycles, and tore down barricades and trenches. That cleared National Road Five, which had been blocked for years. Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked everyone involved in a post on X. The Sri Lankan teams are based in places like Port-au-Prince and Gonaïves, where they patrol in armoured vehicles, protect supply routes, and help local police break up organized crime and bring stability back to communities.
